extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO staff handling patent correspondence
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formatting requirements for preparing, delivering, and filing correspondence, drawings, petitions, and other papers relating to U.S. patent applications (including facsimile and hand-delivery rules). Covers required headings, identifying indicia, delivery routing, Express Mail, fax rules, and signature/certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper heading for incoming papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Incoming papers pertaining to a filed application should carry specific identifying items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to include: (1) Application number (checked for accuracy, including series code and serial no.); (2) Art Unit number (copied from most recent Office communication); (3) Filing date; (4) Name of the examiner who prepared the most recent Office action; (5) Title of invention; (6) Confirmation number (see MPEP § 503). The Office prefers these identifying indicia be provided on drawings; applicants may be reminded by including form paragraph 5.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying indicia on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia, if provided on drawings, must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identifying indicia should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, application number, and confirmation number (see 37 CFR 1.84(c) and MPEP references). If the Office has not yet assigned an application and confirmation number, provide the applicant's docket number (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of replacement and new drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of the application must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When replacement sheets of drawings are submitted after filing, a cover letter identifying the drawings by application number should accompany them. Identification must comply with 37 CFR 1.84(c) and 37 CFR 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defer supplemental submissions until application number assigned
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of additional or supplemental papers on a newly filed application should be deferred until an application number has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is requested to assist Office processing and matching of incoming papers to application files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing non-time-sensitive documents with statutory replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents with no particular time or sequence requirements should be filed with materials submitted in reply to statutory or regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: certified copies of foreign documents to support priority, changes of power of attorney, or changes in mailing address following first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance correspondence routing and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-allowance correspondence, except for petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c), should be addressed 'Mail Stop Issue Fee'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c) to withdraw an application from issue after payment of the issue fee must be clearly marked 'Petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c)' and hand-carried to the Office of Petitions or faxed to the Office of Petitions at (571) 273-0025. Any paper filed after receiving the Issue notification should include the indicated patent number. Because an allowed application may issue within ~4 weeks of payment of the issue fee, post-allowance correspondence should be filed prior to the date of issue fee payment to ensure consideration before issuance. See MPEP § 2732 for patent term adjustment impacts of submitting papers after notice of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized hand-delivery requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No official paper relating to a pending application may be personally delivered to a Technology Center (TC); hand-carried patent application-related correspondence must be delivered to the Customer Service Window, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Dec 1, 2003, all official patent application related correspondence for organizations reporting to the Commissioner for Patents that is hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Service Window, except for certain categories listed (see exceptions entry). Before hand-carrying to a specific office, call to obtain current location; bringing correspondence to the Customer Service Window will be accepted and routed but may incur delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to centralized hand-delivery (permitted hand-delivery locations and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of correspondence may be hand-carried directly to specific USPTO offices/locations instead of the Customer Service Window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated exceptions include: (A) Access Requests — File Information Unit (FIU) or Public Search Facility; (B) Patent Term Extensions under 35 U.S.C. 156 — OPLA; (C) Assignments to be Recorded — Office of Public Records Customer Service Window; (D) Office of General Counsel — specified room; (E) Solicitor’s Office — specified room; (F) Interference related correspondence — drop-off box in Madison East lobby or Room 9B55-A with magnetometer and x-ray screening, time limits and return receipt procedures explained; (G) Secrecy Order correspondence — Licensing and Review (Knox Building); (H) Expedited Foreign Filing License Petitions — drop-off box at Knox guard station with scanning and requirement to provide fax/phone/mail address; (I) Petitions to Withdraw from Issue — Office of Petitions (hand-carried accepted between 8:30 am and 3:45 pm); (J) Documents requested by Office of Patent Publication — specified room; (K) OED — receptionist room; (L) Office of Finance — specific receptionist location with instructions to place envelope labeled REFUND, DEPOSIT ACCOUNT, or MAINTENANCE FEE and note that receptionist will only date-stamp postcard receipt; (M) Office of Public Records — Customer Service Window for certified copy requests. Guidance includes telephone numbers, hours, and special procedures where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail service rules for USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the U.S. Postal Service 'Post Office to Addressee' Express Mail service may be used for mail directed to the USPTO; 'Post Office to Post Office' is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.10 — use of mailing label that indicates deposit date; addresses per 37 CFR 1.1 and MPEP § 501. 'Post Office to Post Office' Express Mail is retained at the postal facility for pickup and the Postal Service does not notify the addressee; USPTO does not pick up mail, so such mail will not reach USPTO (held 15 days then returned). See MPEP § 513 for Express Mail mailing procedure of 37 CFR 1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission general receipt rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence (except proscribed categories) may be transmitted by facsimile; the receipt date is the date the complete transmission is received by USPTO unless that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or District of Columbia Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate proper processing, each transmission session should be limited to correspondence to be filed in a single application or proceeding. The application number, reexamination control number, interference number, or patent number should be entered on the facsimile cover sheet as part of sender identification. If transmission completes on a weekend/holiday, the receipt date is the next succeeding business day. Use of a Certificate of Transmission (for documents not proscribed by 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2)) may allow timeliness to be accorded to an earlier date if in compliance with 37 CFR 1.8(a)(1)(i)(B) and (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission prohibitions (when faxing is not permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile transmissions are not permitted and, if submitted, will not be accorded a date of receipt in specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited situations include: (1) Correspondence requiring an original signature as in § 1.4(e); (2) Certified documents as in § 1.4(f); (3) Correspondence which cannot receive the benefit of the certificate of mailing or transmission as specified in § 1.8(a)(2)(i)(A)-(D) and (F), and § 1.8(a)(2)(iii)(A) (with limited continued prosecution application exception); (4) Color drawings submitted under listed drawing rules (e.g., §§ 1.81, 1.83-1.85, etc.); (5) A request for reexamination under § 1.510 or § 1.913; (6) Correspondence to be filed in a patent application subject to a secrecy order under §§ 5.1–5.5 and directly related to secrecy order content; (7)-(8) [Reserved]; (9) In contested cases before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences except as the Board may expressly authorize. Senders are cautioned against submitting proscribed material by facsimile since it will not be accorded a receipt date; the Office will attempt to notify senders when a fax falls within these prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile filing content and examples permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of correspondence that may generally be transmitted by facsimile include several enumerated document types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted types include: continued prosecution applications (CPAs) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) for design apps only, amendments, declarations, petitions, information disclosure statements (IDS), terminal disclaimers, notices of appeal and appeal briefs, requests for continued examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114, assignment documents, issue fee transmittals and authorizations to charge deposit accounts. Prohibitions cover situations requiring originals or where accepting fax would unduly burden the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special CPA-by-fax filing procedures and remedies if USPTO has no evidence of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of a CPA transmitted by facsimile under § 1.53(d), the transmitting party may petition the Director to accord a filing date as of the transmission date, subject to specified requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (i) inform the Office promptly after learning that no evidence of receipt exists; (ii) supply an additional copy of the previously transmitted CPA; (iii) include a statement attesting, on personal knowledge basis or to Director's satisfaction, to the previous transmission and include a copy of the sending unit’s report confirming transmission or equivalent evidence created after the transmission and within one business day. The Office may require additional evidence to determine if transmission and receipt occurred on the date in question. There is also a special receipt procedure whereby the Office will fax back a receipt of a CPA filing if applicant submits the Office receipt form along with the CPA filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized facsimile number and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Dec 1, 2003, all patent application related correspondence transmitted by facsimile must be directed to the central facsimile number (571) 273-8300, with certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to Office actions including after-final amendments transmitted by facsimile must be directed to the central facsimile number. Unofficial correspondence (draft proposed amendments for interviews) may still be sent to Technology Centers. Office personnel should not use personal fax numbers for official correspondence; if they inadvertently receive official correspondence, they must route (not forward) it to the central number or, with applicant permission, make it part of an examiner's amendment. Certain operations/offices have specific facsimile numbers for particular permitted correspondence (see separate entry for list of locations and numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted alternative facsimile numbers and limited types of correspondence per office
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific USPTO offices/units have individual facsimile numbers that may be used for particular types of correspondence; other correspondence must go to the central number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (not exhaustive): PCT Operations (papers in international applications) — (571) 273-3201; Office of Patent Publication (issue fee & publication fee payments) — (571) 273-2885; Pre-Grant Publication petitions — (703) 305-8568; Electronic Business Center (customer number data change requests) — (571) 273-0177; Assignment Branch — (571) 273-0140 (assignment rules and limitations apply); Central Reexamination Unit — (571) 273-9900 (except initial request); Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences — (571) 273-0042 (only where expressly authorized); Office of the General Counsel — (571) 273-0099; Solicitor — (571) 273-0373; Licensing and Review — (571) 273-0185 (for foreign filing license petitions; secrecy-order-related correspondence still prohibited); Office of Petitions — (571) 273-0025 (petitions to withdraw from issue). Additional numbers for OED, Office of Finance, Office of Public Records, etc., are provided with customer service telephone numbers and restrictions. For each location, only the particular types indicated may be transmitted; all other types must go to the central number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories where facsimile filing is not permitted (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of categories of documents and proceedings where filing by facsimile transmission is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (A) documents required by statute to be certified; (B) national patent application specification and drawings for obtaining an application filing date (provisional or nonprovisional) except CPAs under § 1.53(d); (C) color drawings submitted under designated drawing rules; (D) correspondence in an interference ordered to be filed by hand or Express Mail; (E) agreements between parties to an interference under 35 U.S.C. 135(c); (F) correspondence in contested Board cases unless Board authorizes; (G) correspondence in applications subject to secrecy orders directly related to secrecy content; (H) an international application for patent; (I) a copy of the international application plus basic national fee to enter national stage (37 CFR 1.495(b)); (J) a request for reexamination under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.913. Applicants are reminded that facsimile may reduce drawing quality and the Office will generally print drawings as received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature types and requirements for correspondence (§ 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence requiring a person's signature may be filed with one of three types of signatures: (A) handwritten signature (original), (B) S-signature, or (C) EFS character coded signature, subject to conditions and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handwritten signature: must be an original handwritten signature personally signed in permanent dark ink (or a direct/indirect copy such as photocopy or facsimile of an original — if a copy is filed the original should be retained; Office may require original for authenticity). S-signature: signature inserted between forward slashes (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/), may consist only of letters and Arabic numerals and punctuation; patent practitioners signing under §§ 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(2) must supply registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature; the signer’s name should be printed/typed adjacent and be specific enough to identify signer. EFS character coded signature: for filings via the Office Electronic Filing System the electronic signature must consist only of letters of the English alphabet or Arabic numerals (with permitted punctuation) and be inserted between forward slashes. Correspondence requiring a person’s signature relating to registration practice, enrollment/disciplinary investigations, or disciplinary proceedings must be submitted with an original handwritten signature. When statute requires certification, a copy/photocopy/facsimile of the certification is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and sanctions related to signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of any paper to the Office constitutes a certification under § 10.18(b); there are obligations and potential sanctions concerning signatures and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications as to signature 'of another': a submitter must have a reasonable basis to believe a signature was actually inserted by that person and retain evidence of authenticity. 'Self certification': the person inserting an S-signature or EFS signature certifies that the signature is their own. Violations of certification rules may result in sanctions under § 10.18(c) and (d) and disciplinary action for practitioners. The Office may require ratification, confirmation (including submitting a duplicate document with proper signature), or other evidence of authenticity when there is reasonable doubt (e.g., signature variations or mismatch with typed name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature authenticity and Office remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a signature is required, the Office may require evidence of authenticity and may accept copies only under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each piece of correspondence requiring a signature must either be an original handwritten signature in permanent dark ink or be a direct/indirect copy (photocopy or fax) of an original; if a copy is filed, the original should be retained. If authenticity is questioned, the Office may require submission of the original, ratification, or other evidence. Signatures for registration practice/disciplines must be original handwritten signatures.
